<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-md-req-end-065-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings"></div>

# [REQ-END-065] Configure Network Inspection System (NIS) settings

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: Medium
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Network Inspection System`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\NIS`
      * `EnableConvertWarnToBlock` = `1` (REG_DWORD)
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\NIS`
      * `AllowSwitchToAsyncInspection` = `1` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
The Network Inspection System (NIS) inspects network traffic patterns for known exploits. Converting warning verdicts to block enforces inline blocking of zero-day exploits, while allowing async inspection prevents performance overhead from slowing local network interfaces.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
None.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Network Inspection System
2. Set 'Convert warn verdict to block' to 'Enabled'
3. Set 'Turn on asynchronous inspection' to 'Enabled'

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>

### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-DefenderNis.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-DefenderNis.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-DefenderNis.ps1
$NisPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\NIS"
if (-not (Test-Path $NisPath)) { New-Item -Path $NisPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $NisPath -Name "EnableConvertWarnToBlock" -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $NisPath -Name "AllowSwitchToAsyncInspection" -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-DefenderNisStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-DefenderNisStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-DefenderNisStatus.ps1
$Reg = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\NIS" -Name "EnableConvertWarnToBlock" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$RegAsync = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\NIS" -Name "AllowSwitchToAsyncInspection" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if (($Reg -and $Reg.EnableConvertWarnToBlock -eq 1) -and ($RegAsync -and $RegAsync.AllowSwitchToAsyncInspection -eq 1)) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

---

# [REQ-END-066] Configure OOBE Real-Time Protection and Security Intelligence

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-oobe-real-time-protection-and-security-intelligence-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-oobe-real-time-protection-and-security-intelligence-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: Medium
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Real-time Protection`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Real-Time Protection`
      * `OobeEnableRtpAndSigUpdate` = `1` (REG_DWORD)

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-oobe-real-time-protection-and-security-intelligence-md-rationale"></div>

Enabling real-time protection and intelligence updates during the Out-of-Box Experience (OOBE) ensures that the system is fully updated and protected before the initial administrative user signs in or connects to enterprise network nodes.

# [REQ-END-067] Enable Dynamic Signature Dropped Event Reporting

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-enable-dynamic-signature-dropped-event-reporting-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-enable-dynamic-signature-dropped-event-reporting-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: Low
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Reporting`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Reporting`
      * `EnableDynamicSignatureDroppedEventReporting` = `1` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-enable-dynamic-signature-dropped-event-reporting-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Enabling this log report generation triggers explicit events when a dynamic scan ruleset signature is dropped. This ensures SIEM integrations can immediately log changes in the local threat signatures dataset.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-enable-dynamic-signature-dropped-event-reporting-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
None.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-enable-dynamic-signature-dropped-event-reporting-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Reporting
2. Set 'Configure whether to report Dynamic Signature dropped events' to 'Enabled'

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-enable-dynamic-signature-dropped-event-reporting-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>

### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-md-req-end-068-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions"></div>

# [REQ-END-068] Configure Quick Scan and Scanning Exclusions

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: Medium
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Scan`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan`
      * `QuickScanIncludeExclusions` = `1` (REG_DWORD)
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan`
      * `DisablePackedExeScanning` = `0` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Malware frequently tries to establish persistence in excluded directories or inside packed/compressed executables. Forcing quick scans to include excluded files and ensuring packed file structures are recursively scanned prevents malware evasion.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Increased quick scan times depending on folder sizes and compression ratios.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Scan
2. Set 'Scan excluded files and directories during quick scans' to 'Enabled'
3. Set 'Turn off scanning of packed executables' to 'Disabled'

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>

### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-DefenderQuickScan.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-DefenderQuickScan.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-DefenderQuickScan.ps1
Set-MpPreference -DisablePackedExeScanning $false
$ScanPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan"
if (-not (Test-Path $ScanPath)) { New-Item -Path $ScanPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ScanPath -Name "QuickScanIncludeExclusions" -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ScanPath -Name "DisablePackedExeScanning" -Value 0 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-DefenderQuickScanStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-DefenderQuickScanStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-DefenderQuickScanStatus.ps1
$Pref = Get-MpPreference
$Reg = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan" -Name "QuickScanIncludeExclusions" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$RegPack = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan" -Name "DisablePackedExeScanning" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if (($Pref.DisablePackedExeScanning -eq $false -or ($RegPack -and $RegPack.DisablePackedExeScanning -eq 0)) -and
    ($Reg -and $Reg.QuickScanIncludeExclusions -eq 1)) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters-md-req-end-069-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters"></div>

# [REQ-END-069] Configure Scheduled Scan Parameters

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: Medium
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Scan`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan`
      * `ScheduleDay` = `0` (REG_DWORD)
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan`
      * `DisableEmailScanning` = `0` (REG_DWORD)
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan`
      * `DisableHeuristics` = `0` (REG_DWORD)
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan`
      * `DaysWithoutCatchupQuickScan` = `7` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Ensuring daily scheduled scans, enabling heuristics for behavioral anomaly detection, scan mail attachments, and forcing a catchup scan after at most 7 days ensures system integrity is continually validated.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Slight scanning overhead.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Scan
2. Set 'Specify the day of the week to run a scheduled scan' to 'Enabled' (Select 'Every day' or '0')
3. Set 'Turn on e-mail scanning' to 'Enabled'
4. Set 'Turn on heuristics' to 'Enabled'
5. Set 'Trigger a quick scan after X days without any scans' to 'Enabled' (7 days)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>

### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-DefenderScheduledScan.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-DefenderScheduledScan.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-DefenderScheduledScan.ps1
Set-MpPreference -DisableEmailScanning $false
Set-MpPreference -DisableHeuristics $false
$ScanPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan"
if (-not (Test-Path $ScanPath)) { New-Item -Path $ScanPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ScanPath -Name "ScheduleDay" -Value 0 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ScanPath -Name "DisableEmailScanning" -Value 0 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ScanPath -Name "DisableHeuristics" -Value 0 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ScanPath -Name "DaysWithoutCatchupQuickScan" -Value 7 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-DefenderScheduledScanStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-DefenderScheduledScanStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-DefenderScheduledScanStatus.ps1
$Pref = Get-MpPreference
$RegDays = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan" -Name "DaysWithoutCatchupQuickScan" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($Pref.DisableEmailScanning -eq $false -and $Pref.DisableHeuristics -eq $false -and ($RegDays -and $RegDays.DaysWithoutCatchupQuickScan -eq 7)) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule-md-req-end-070-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule"></div>

# [REQ-END-070] Configure Security Intelligence Update Schedule

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: Medium
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Security Intelligence Updates`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Signature Updates`
      * `ASSignatureDue` = `7` (REG_DWORD)
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Signature Updates`
      * `AVSignatureDue` = `7` (REG_DWORD)
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Signature Updates`
      * `ScheduleDay` = `0` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Antivirus signatures must remain fresh to block the latest published threats. Mandating daily checks for updates and marking signatures older than 7 days as out-of-date ensures continuous defense parity.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Requires continuous outbound connectivity to WSUS or Microsoft Update endpoints.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Security Intelligence Updates
2. Set 'Define the number of days before spyware security intelligence is considered out of date' to 'Enabled' (7 days)
3. Set 'Define the number of days before virus security intelligence is considered out of date' to 'Enabled' (7 days)
4. Set 'Specify the day of the week to check for security intelligence updates' to 'Enabled' (Every day or 0)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>

### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-DefenderUpdateSchedule.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-DefenderUpdateSchedule.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-DefenderUpdateSchedule.ps1
$SigPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Signature Updates"
if (-not (Test-Path $SigPath)) { New-Item -Path $SigPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $SigPath -Name "ASSignatureDue" -Value 7 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $SigPath -Name "AVSignatureDue" -Value 7 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $SigPath -Name "ScheduleDay" -Value 0 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-DefenderUpdateScheduleStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-DefenderUpdateScheduleStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-DefenderUpdateScheduleStatus.ps1
$Reg = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Signature Updates" -Name "ASSignatureDue" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$RegAV = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Signature Updates" -Name "AVSignatureDue" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$RegDay = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Signature Updates" -Name "ScheduleDay" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if (($Reg -and $Reg.ASSignatureDue -eq 7) -and ($RegAV -and $RegAV.AVSignatureDue -eq 7) -and ($RegDay -and $RegDay.ScheduleDay -eq 0)) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-attack-surface-reduction-rules-md"></div>

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-attack-surface-reduction-rules-md-configure-attack-surface-reduction-rules"></div>

# Configure Attack Surface Reduction Rules

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-attack-surface-reduction-rules-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-attack-surface-reduction-rules-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-attack-surface-reduction-rules-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules targets software behaviors that are frequently abused by malware, such as launching executable files from email attachments, spawning child processes from Office apps or PDF viewers, credential theft from LSASS, and writing unsigned files from USB.

This submodule contains individual requirement rules for each ASR control enforced on standard workstations.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-attack-surface-reduction-rules-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
* **Detailed Audit Phase**: ASR rules should first be deployed in **Audit** mode to collect telemetry in the Windows Event Logs (Event ID `1121` or `1122`). This allows administrators to configure exclusions before switching to **Block** mode (`1`).
* **Macro/Office Dependencies**: Organizations relying on advanced inter-process Office communication or macros running system API calls will experience disruptions. Software configurations or ASR exclusion groups must be updated.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-attack-surface-reduction-rules-md-enforced-attack-surface-reduction-rules"></div>

## Enforced Attack Surface Reduction Rules

The following individual ASR rules must be configured in Block mode:

1. **[REQ-END-080 - ASR: Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers](#08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md)**
2. **[REQ-END-081 - ASR: Block Adobe Reader from creating child processes](#08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-adobe-reader-child-processes-md)**
3. **[REQ-END-082 - ASR: Block all Office applications from creating child processes](#08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-child-processes-md)**
4. **[REQ-END-083 - ASR: Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem](#08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-lsass-credential-stealing-md)**
5. **[REQ-END-084 - ASR: Block executable content from email client and webmail](#08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-email-executable-content-md)**
6. **[REQ-END-085 - ASR: Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion](#08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-low-prevalence-executable-files-md)**
7. **[REQ-END-086 - ASR: Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts](#08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-obfuscated-scripts-md)**
8. **[REQ-END-087 - ASR: Block JavaScript or VBScript from launching downloaded executable content](#08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-script-launching-downloaded-content-md)**
9. **[REQ-END-088 - ASR: Block Office applications from creating executable content](#08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-executable-content-creation-md)**
10. **[REQ-END-089 - ASR: Block Office applications from injecting code into other processes](#08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-code-injection-md)**
11. **[REQ-END-090 - ASR: Block Office communication application from creating child processes](#08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-communication-child-processes-md)**
12. **[REQ-END-091 - ASR: Block persistence through WMI event subscription](#08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md)**
13. **[REQ-END-092 - ASR: Block process creations originating from PSExec and WMI commands](#08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-psexec-wmi-process-creations-md)**
14. **[REQ-END-093 - ASR: Block untrusted and unsigned processes that run from USB](#08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-unsigned-processes-running-from-usb-md)**
15. **[REQ-END-094 - ASR: Block Win32 API calls from Office macros](#08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-win32-api-calls-from-office-macros-md)**
16. **[REQ-END-095 - ASR: Use advanced protection against ransomware](#08-endpoints-defender-asr-use-advanced-protection-against-ransomware-md)**

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md"></div>

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md-req-end-080-asr-block-abuse-of-exploited-vulnerable-signed-drivers"></div>

# [REQ-END-080] ASR: Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `56a863a9-875e-4185-98a7-b882c64b5ce5` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Prevents an application from writing a vulnerable signed driver to disk. Attackers use Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) techniques to bypass Windows kernel protections by loading legitimate, signed third-party drivers that contain known vulnerabilities, allowing them to disable security agents and gain kernel-level privileges.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Administrators or developers who deliberately load older or specific signed debugging/hardware diagnostics drivers containing known security bugs will be blocked. Approvals or exclusions must be configured for these specific drivers.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction
2. Set 'Configure Attack Surface Reduction rules' to 'Enabled'
3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `56a863a9-875e-4185-98a7-b882c64b5ce5` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>

### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-AsrVulnerableDrivers.ps1](../../implementation_scripts/Configure-AsrVulnerableDrivers.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-AsrVulnerableDrivers.ps1
$AsrRulesPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules"
if (-not (Test-Path $AsrRulesPath)) { New-Item -Path $AsrRulesPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $AsrRulesPath -Name "56a863a9-875e-4185-98a7-b882c64b5ce5" -Value "1" -Type String -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-AsrVulnerableDriversStatus.ps1](../../audit_scripts/Get-AsrVulnerableDriversStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-AsrVulnerableDriversStatus.ps1
$AsrRulesPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules"
$Value = Get-ItemProperty -Path $AsrRulesPath -Name "56a863a9-875e-4185-98a7-b882c64b5ce5" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($Value -and ($Value."56a863a9-875e-4185-98a7-b882c64b5ce5" -eq "1" -or $Value."56a863a9-875e-4185-98a7-b882c64b5ce5" -eq 1)) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-adobe-reader-child-processes-md-req-end-081-asr-block-adobe-reader-from-creating-child-processes"></div>

# [REQ-END-081] ASR: Block Adobe Reader from creating child processes

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-adobe-reader-child-processes-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-adobe-reader-child-processes-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `7674ba52-37eb-4a4f-a9a1-f0f9a1619a2c` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-adobe-reader-child-processes-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Prevents Adobe Reader from launching any child processes. Malicious PDF documents frequently attempt to exploit application vulnerabilities or trick users into executing embedded links, which spawns command shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or scripting hosts (wscript.exe) to download and launch secondary malware payloads.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-adobe-reader-child-processes-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Adobe Reader will be unable to launch external helper applications directly. PDF forms that rely on spawning external applications or customized plugins that execute command-line helpers will fail to run.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-adobe-reader-child-processes-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-adobe-reader-child-processes-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

2. Set 'Configure Attack Surface Reduction rules' to 'Enabled'
3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `7674ba52-37eb-4a4f-a9a1-f0f9a1619a2c` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-adobe-reader-child-processes-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>

if (-not (Test-Path $AsrRulesPath)) { New-Item -Path $AsrRulesPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $AsrRulesPath -Name "7674ba52-37eb-4a4f-a9a1-f0f9a1619a2c" -Value "1" -Type String -Force
```

# [REQ-END-082] ASR: Block all Office applications from creating child processes

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-child-processes-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-child-processes-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `d4f940ab-401b-4efc-aadc-ad5f3c50688a` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-child-processes-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Blocks Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) from creating child processes. This prevents malicious files containing embedded VBA macros or exploiting unpatched vulnerabilities (such as CVE-2021-40444) from launching scripting environments or system commands to download and execute code.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-child-processes-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Office macros that legitimately launch external scripts, shell scripts, or third-party executable helpers will be blocked. Business processes relying on advanced inter-process macros must be rewritten to use modern API alternatives.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-child-processes-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-child-processes-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `d4f940ab-401b-4efc-aadc-ad5f3c50688a` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

---

Set-ItemProperty -Path $AsrRulesPath -Name "d4f940ab-401b-4efc-aadc-ad5f3c50688a" -Value "1" -Type String -Force
```

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-lsass-credential-stealing-md-req-end-083-asr-block-credential-stealing-from-the-windows-local-security-authority-subsystem"></div>

# [REQ-END-083] ASR: Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-lsass-credential-stealing-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-lsass-credential-stealing-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `9e6c4e1f-7d60-472f-ba1a-a39ef669e4b2` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-lsass-credential-stealing-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Blocks attempts to open or dump the memory of the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (lsass.exe). Attackers dump LSASS memory using tools like Mimikatz or Task Manager to extract plaintext credentials, Kerberos tickets, or NTLM password hashes from system memory for lateral movement.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-lsass-credential-stealing-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Administrative diagnostic tools, customized authentication packages, or security scanners that attempt to open the LSASS process handle to read user tokens or perform access auditing will be blocked.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-lsass-credential-stealing-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-lsass-credential-stealing-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)

2. Set 'Configure Attack Surface Reduction rules' to 'Enabled'
3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `9e6c4e1f-7d60-472f-ba1a-a39ef669e4b2` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-lsass-credential-stealing-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>

if (-not (Test-Path $AsrRulesPath)) { New-Item -Path $AsrRulesPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $AsrRulesPath -Name "9e6c4e1f-7d60-472f-ba1a-a39ef669e4b2" -Value "1" -Type String -Force

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-email-executable-content-md-req-end-084-asr-block-executable-content-from-email-client-and-webmail"></div>

# [REQ-END-084] ASR: Block executable content from email client and webmail

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-email-executable-content-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-email-executable-content-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `be9ba2d9-53ea-4cdc-84e5-9b1eeee46550` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-email-executable-content-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Prevents executable files (such as .exe, .com, .scr, .vbs, .js, or .pif) from launching directly from email clients (like Outlook) or webmail accessed via browser sessions. This stops phishing attacks where users accidentally launch malicious attachments or download payloads directly from web-based email links.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-email-executable-content-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Users will be blocked from directly launching attachments that contain scripts, setup files, or macros. They must first save the file to an authorized directory and run it from there (which allows standard real-time scans to run first).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-email-executable-content-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-email-executable-content-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction
2. Set 'Configure Attack Surface Reduction rules' to 'Enabled'
3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `be9ba2d9-53ea-4cdc-84e5-9b1eeee46550` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-low-prevalence-executable-files-md-req-end-085-asr-block-executable-files-from-running-unless-they-meet-a-prevalence-age-or-trusted-list-criterion"></div>

# [REQ-END-085] ASR: Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-low-prevalence-executable-files-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-low-prevalence-executable-files-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `01443614-cd74-433a-b99e-2ecdc07bfc25` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-low-prevalence-executable-files-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Blocks execution of unrecognized, newly compiled, or low-prevalence executable files. This provides initial protection against zero-day malware campaigns and targeted custom payloads that have not yet established reputation telemetry in the Microsoft Cloud Protection network.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-low-prevalence-executable-files-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Developers building and testing custom internal binaries, or administrators installing niche, uncertified third-party software updates will face false positives. Exclusions must be configured for target test directories.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-low-prevalence-executable-files-md-implementation-steps"></div>

3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `01443614-cd74-433a-b99e-2ecdc07bfc25` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

---

# [REQ-END-086] ASR: Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-obfuscated-scripts-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-obfuscated-scripts-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `5beb7efe-fd9a-4556-801d-275e5ffc04cc` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-obfuscated-scripts-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Blocks execution of obfuscated or encrypted scripts (such as PowerShell, VBScript, or JavaScript). Threat actors obfuscate their scripts using base64 encoding, custom string manipulation, or encryption to hide the intent of their code and bypass static file scanning and network detection engines.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-obfuscated-scripts-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Legitimate administrative tools or third-party provisioning scripts that use heavy minification, obfuscation, or custom encoding wrappers will be blocked. Scripts must be refactored to use readable, signed code.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-obfuscated-scripts-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `5beb7efe-fd9a-4556-801d-275e5ffc04cc` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

---

# [REQ-END-087] ASR: Block JavaScript or VBScript from launching downloaded executable content

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-script-launching-downloaded-content-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-script-launching-downloaded-content-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `d3e037e1-3eb8-44c8-a917-57927947596d` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-script-launching-downloaded-content-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Prevents JavaScript or VBScript running locally from launching executable binaries that were downloaded from the internet. Attackers use malicious scripts inside documents or web browsers to download payloads (like ransomware or trojans) to the disk and launch them using local script engines.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-script-launching-downloaded-content-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Local administrative script engines that perform software deployment or download updates and then launch installers will be blocked. These scripts must be replaced by structured configuration agents or signed installers.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-script-launching-downloaded-content-md-implementation-steps"></div>

# [REQ-END-088] ASR: Block Office applications from creating executable content

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-executable-content-creation-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-executable-content-creation-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `3b576869-a4ec-4529-8536-b80a7769e899` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-executable-content-creation-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Prevents Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) from creating or writing executable files (e.g., .exe, .dll, .scr) to the local filesystem. Malicious documents often attempt to drop payloads directly into the local temp folders or AppData directories before executing them.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-executable-content-creation-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Macros or add-ins that legitimately save external binaries or compile executable helper objects locally will be blocked.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-executable-content-creation-md-implementation-steps"></div>

3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `3b576869-a4ec-4529-8536-b80a7769e899` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

# [REQ-END-089] ASR: Block Office applications from injecting code into other processes

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-code-injection-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-code-injection-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `75668c1f-73b5-4cf0-bb93-3ecf5cb7cc84` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-code-injection-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Blocks Microsoft Office applications from writing code or injecting threads directly into external processes. Threat actors use code injection (such as process hollowing or remote thread creation) inside Office macros to hide execution under clean, trusted system binaries like explorer.exe or svchost.exe.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-code-injection-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Office plugins or custom integration tools that inject threads or communicate with database engines using active injection libraries will be blocked.

---

      * `26190899-1602-49e8-8b27-eb1d0a1ce869` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-communication-child-processes-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Blocks Microsoft Outlook or other Office communication applications (e.g., Teams, Skype) from creating child processes. This prevents malware payloads delivered through emails, chats, or calendar invites from spawning command-line utilities or scripting environments.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-communication-child-processes-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Outlook integrations or custom add-ins that legitimately spawn helper utilities, such as starting external browsers or custom document handlers directly, may be blocked.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-office-communication-child-processes-md-implementation-steps"></div>

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md-req-end-091-asr-block-persistence-through-wmi-event-subscription"></div>

# [REQ-END-091] ASR: Block persistence through WMI event subscription

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `e6db77e5-3df2-4cf1-b95a-636979351e5b` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Blocks threat actors from achieving system persistence by registering permanent Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) event subscriptions. WMI event subscriptions allow attackers to automatically launch malicious payloads when system triggers occur (like system boot or user logon) without using traditional startup registry keys.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Management software or diagnostic monitoring tools that legitimately register permanent WMI event filters to track system telemetry will be blocked. Alternatives like Windows services or scheduled tasks must be used.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

2. Set 'Configure Attack Surface Reduction rules' to 'Enabled'
3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `e6db77e5-3df2-4cf1-b95a-636979351e5b` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>

Set-ItemProperty -Path $AsrRulesPath -Name "e6db77e5-3df2-4cf1-b95a-636979351e5b" -Value "1" -Type String -Force

# [REQ-END-092] ASR: Block process creations originating from PSExec and WMI commands

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-psexec-wmi-process-creations-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-psexec-wmi-process-creations-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `d1e49aac-8f56-4280-b9ba-993a6d77406c` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-psexec-wmi-process-creations-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Blocks processes created via WMI commands or PSExec remote execution utilities. This directly stops lateral movement attacks where compromised accounts or threat actors attempt to start commands, backdoors, or credential dumpers remotely across domain-joined servers and workstations.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-psexec-wmi-process-creations-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Disrupts remote administration tools, monitoring agents, and network scanners that rely on WMI/PSExec. For Domain Controllers or critical servers, this rule is often set to **Audit** mode (`2`) rather than hard Block mode (`1`) to prevent administrative downtime.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-psexec-wmi-process-creations-md-implementation-steps"></div>

2. Set 'Configure Attack Surface Reduction rules' to 'Enabled'
3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `d1e49aac-8f56-4280-b9ba-993a6d77406c` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-psexec-wmi-process-creations-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>

Set-ItemProperty -Path $AsrRulesPath -Name "d1e49aac-8f56-4280-b9ba-993a6d77406c" -Value "1" -Type String -Force

# [REQ-END-093] ASR: Block untrusted and unsigned processes that run from USB

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-unsigned-processes-running-from-usb-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-unsigned-processes-running-from-usb-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `b2b3f03d-6a65-4f7b-a9c7-1c7ef74a9ba4` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-unsigned-processes-running-from-usb-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Blocks the execution of unsigned or untrusted processes on removable storage devices (USB drives, external SSDs). This stops physical access vectors, rogue USB drops, and automated worm propagation techniques from running unauthorized installers or scripts.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-unsigned-processes-running-from-usb-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Administrators or developers will be unable to run unsigned utilities directly from portable flash drives. Software must be copied to local trusted storage, or the binary must possess a trusted digital signature.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-unsigned-processes-running-from-usb-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-unsigned-processes-running-from-usb-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `b2b3f03d-6a65-4f7b-a9c7-1c7ef74a9ba4` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-win32-api-calls-from-office-macros-md-req-end-094-asr-block-win32-api-calls-from-office-macros"></div>

# [REQ-END-094] ASR: Block Win32 API calls from Office macros

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-win32-api-calls-from-office-macros-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-win32-api-calls-from-office-macros-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `92e97fa1-2edf-4476-bdd6-9dd0b4dddc7b` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-win32-api-calls-from-office-macros-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Blocks VBA macros inside Microsoft Office documents from invoking Win32 API calls. Malicious documents use macros to call kernel memory functions (such as VirtualAlloc, WriteProcessMemory, or CreateThread) to load and execute shellcode in memory without dropping files to disk, bypassing file scanners.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-win32-api-calls-from-office-macros-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Advanced business spreadsheets or database documents that utilize Win32 API calls for custom UI rendering, network calls, or system commands will fail. They must be rewritten using standard secure VBA structures or add-in APIs.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-win32-api-calls-from-office-macros-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-block-win32-api-calls-from-office-macros-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `92e97fa1-2edf-4476-bdd6-9dd0b4dddc7b` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

---

if (-not (Test-Path $AsrRulesPath)) { New-Item -Path $AsrRulesPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $AsrRulesPath -Name "92e97fa1-2edf-4476-bdd6-9dd0b4dddc7b" -Value "1" -Type String -Force
```

# [REQ-END-095] ASR: Use advanced protection against ransomware

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-use-advanced-protection-against-ransomware-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-use-advanced-protection-against-ransomware-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `c1db55ab-c21a-4637-bb3f-a12568109d35` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-use-advanced-protection-against-ransomware-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Enables advanced behavioral heuristics and cloud analytics checks on files that attempt to modify multiple user files, detect signature-less encryption behavior, and block rapid write activity to prevent ransomware from encrypting system and user documents.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-asr-use-advanced-protection-against-ransomware-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Minor performance overhead when scanning active files during large batch edits or heavy database updates.

---

$AsrRulesPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules"
$Value = Get-ItemProperty -Path $AsrRulesPath -Name "c1db55ab-c21a-4637-bb3f-a12568109d35" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($Value -and ($Value."c1db55ab-c21a-4637-bb3f-a12568109d35" -eq "1" -or $Value."c1db55ab-c21a-4637-bb3f-a12568109d35" -eq 1)) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-threat-severity-default-quarantine-actions-md"></div>

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-threat-severity-default-quarantine-actions-md-req-end-072-configure-threat-severity-default-quarantine-actions"></div>

# [REQ-END-072] Configure Threat Severity Default Quarantine Actions

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-threat-severity-default-quarantine-actions-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-threat-severity-default-quarantine-actions-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: Medium
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Threats`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Threats`
      * `Threats_ThreatSeverityDefaultAction` = `1` (REG_DWORD)
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Threats\ThreatSeverityDefaultAction`
      * `1` = `2` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-threat-severity-default-quarantine-actions-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
By default, Defender may prompt users or take actions (like clean/ignore) that leave malware remnants on the filesystem. Configuring default quarantine actions for all severities (low, medium, high, severe) ensures automated containment.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-threat-severity-default-quarantine-actions-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
None.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-threat-severity-default-quarantine-actions-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-threat-severity-default-quarantine-actions-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Threats
2. Set 'Specify threat alert levels at which default action should not be taken when detected' to 'Enabled'
3. Click 'Show...' and enter threat levels (1 -> 2, 2 -> 2, 4 -> 2, 5 -> 2)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-threat-severity-default-quarantine-actions-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>

### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-DefenderThreatActions.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-DefenderThreatActions.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-DefenderThreatActions.ps1
$ThreatsPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Threats"
if (-not (Test-Path $ThreatsPath)) { New-Item -Path $ThreatsPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ThreatsPath -Name "Threats_ThreatSeverityDefaultAction" -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force
$ThreatsSevPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Threats\ThreatSeverityDefaultAction"
if (-not (Test-Path $ThreatsSevPath)) { New-Item -Path $ThreatsSevPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ThreatsSevPath -Name "1" -Value 2 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ThreatsSevPath -Name "2" -Value 2 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ThreatsSevPath -Name "4" -Value 2 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ThreatsSevPath -Name "5" -Value 2 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-DefenderThreatActionsStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-DefenderThreatActionsStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-DefenderThreatActionsStatus.ps1
$Reg = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Threats" -Name "Threats_ThreatSeverityDefaultAction" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$RegSev = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Threats\ThreatSeverityDefaultAction" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if (($Reg -and $Reg.Threats_ThreatSeverityDefaultAction -eq 1) -and 
    ($RegSev -and $RegSev.1 -eq 2 -and $RegSev.2 -eq 2 -and $RegSev.4 -eq 2 -and $RegSev.5 -eq 2)) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-threat-severity-default-quarantine-actions-md-sources-compliance-references"></div>

* **CIS Microsoft Windows 10 Benchmark**: Section 18.9 (Windows Defender Antivirus configuration parameters)
* **ANSSI Active Directory Hardening Guide**: Protective controls baselines on client workstations

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-family-options-ui-lockdown-md-req-end-073-configure-family-options-ui-lockdown"></div>

# [REQ-END-073] Configure Family Options UI Lockdown

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-family-options-ui-lockdown-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-family-options-ui-lockdown-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: Low
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Security\Family options`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender Security Center\Family options`
      * `UILockdown` = `1` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-family-options-ui-lockdown-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Locking down non-essential components of the Windows Security Center interface prevents users from tampering with parental or diagnostic UI controls on enterprise assets.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-family-options-ui-lockdown-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
None.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-family-options-ui-lockdown-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-family-options-ui-lockdown-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Security\Family options
2. Set 'Hide the Family options area' to 'Enabled'

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-family-options-ui-lockdown-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>

### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-DefenderFamilyLockdown.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-DefenderFamilyLockdown.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-DefenderFamilyLockdown.ps1
$FamilyPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender Security Center\Family options"
if (-not (Test-Path $FamilyPath)) { New-Item -Path $FamilyPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $FamilyPath -Name "UILockdown" -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-DefenderFamilyLockdownStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-DefenderFamilyLockdownStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-DefenderFamilyLockdownStatus.ps1
$Reg = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender Security Center\Family options" -Name "UILockdown" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($Reg -and $Reg.UILockdown -eq 1) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-tamper-protection-md"></div>

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-tamper-protection-md-req-end-074-configure-tamper-protection"></div>

# [REQ-END-074] Configure Tamper Protection

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-tamper-protection-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-tamper-protection-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Security\Tamper Protection`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Features`
      * `TamperProtection` = `5` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-tamper-protection-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Tamper Protection prevents local administrators or compromised system accounts from disabling Windows Defender services, real-time scanning, or modifying active exclusions locally. This blocks a primary malware persistence vector.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-tamper-protection-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Local registry modifications to Defender configurations will be ignored. All changes must originate from central templates or cloud console panels.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-tamper-protection-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-tamper-protection-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Security\Tamper Protection
2. Set 'Protect Windows Security settings from tampering' to 'Enabled' (Block or On depending on ADMX version)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-tamper-protection-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>

### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-DefenderTamperProtection.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-DefenderTamperProtection.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-DefenderTamperProtection.ps1
$FeaturesPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Features"
if (-not (Test-Path $FeaturesPath)) { New-Item -Path $FeaturesPath -Force | Out-Null }
try {
    Set-ItemProperty -Path $FeaturesPath -Name "TamperProtection" -Value 5 -Type DWord -ErrorAction Stop -Force
} catch {
    Write-Warning "Registry blocked. Tamper Protection registry key is normally protected by TrustedInstaller. Ensure GPO setting is applied."
}
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-DefenderTamperProtectionStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-DefenderTamperProtectionStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-DefenderTamperProtectionStatus.ps1
$FeaturesPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Features"
$TamperVal = Get-ItemProperty -Path $FeaturesPath -Name "TamperProtection" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($TamperVal -and $TamperVal.TamperProtection -eq 5) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-tamper-protection-md-sources-compliance-references"></div>

* **ANSSI Active Directory Hardening Guide**: Protective controls baselines on client workstations

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-sandbox-execution-environment-md-req-end-075-configure-sandbox-execution-environment"></div>

# [REQ-END-075] Configure Sandbox Execution Environment

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-sandbox-execution-environment-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-sandbox-execution-environment-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Preferences\Windows Settings\Environment`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Environment`
      * `MP_FORCE_USE_SANDBOX` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-sandbox-execution-environment-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Forcing the Windows Defender scanning service (MsMpEng.exe) to run in a restricted AppContainer sandbox prevents privilege escalation. If an attacker exploits a parsing vulnerability in the engine, the compromise is contained inside the sandbox.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-sandbox-execution-environment-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
A system reboot is required to initialize the scanning process within the AppContainer sandbox.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-sandbox-execution-environment-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-sandbox-execution-environment-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Preferences\Windows Settings\Environment
2. Right-click and select New -> Environment Variable
3. Configure Action: Update, Type: System, Name: MP_FORCE_USE_SANDBOX, Value: 1

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-sandbox-execution-environment-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>

### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-DefenderSandbox.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-DefenderSandbox.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-DefenderSandbox.ps1
$EnvPath = "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Environment"
if (-not (Test-Path $EnvPath)) { New-Item -Path $EnvPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $EnvPath -Name "MP_FORCE_USE_SANDBOX" -Value "1" -Type String -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-DefenderSandboxStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-DefenderSandboxStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-DefenderSandboxStatus.ps1
$EnvPath = "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Environment"
$SandboxVar = Get-ItemProperty -Path $EnvPath -Name "MP_FORCE_USE_SANDBOX" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($SandboxVar -and $SandboxVar.MP_FORCE_USE_SANDBOX -eq "1") {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-sandbox-execution-environment-md-sources-compliance-references"></div>

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-amsi-authenticode-signature-verification-md-req-end-076-configure-amsi-authenticode-signature-verification"></div>

# [REQ-END-076] Configure AMSI Authenticode Signature Verification

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-amsi-authenticode-signature-verification-md-target-scope"></div>

## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Tier 2 client workstations and member servers.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 (and above) Enterprise/Professional, Windows Server 2016 (and above).

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-amsi-authenticode-signature-verification-md-implementation-details"></div>

## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Preferences\Windows Settings\Registry`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\AMSI`
      * `FeatureBits` = `2` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-amsi-authenticode-signature-verification-md-rationale"></div>

## Rationale
Enforcing signature checks on registered Antimalware Scan Interface (AMSI) providers blocks attackers from registering unsigned rogue AMSI provider DLLs to bypass script analysis.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-amsi-authenticode-signature-verification-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Third-party antivirus/security providers must register using signed Authenticode binaries to prevent being blocked.

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-amsi-authenticode-signature-verification-md-implementation-steps"></div>

## Implementation Steps

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-amsi-authenticode-signature-verification-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Preferences\Windows Settings\Registry
2. Right-click and select New -> Registry Item
3. Configure Action: Update, Hive: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE, Key Path: SOFTWARE\Microsoft\AMSI, Value Name: FeatureBits, Value Type: REG_DWORD, Value Data: 2

---

<div id="08-endpoints-defender-configure-amsi-authenticode-signature-verification-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>

### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-DefenderAmsiSignature.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-DefenderAmsiSignature.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-DefenderAmsiSignature.ps1
$AmsiPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\AMSI"
if (-not (Test-Path $AmsiPath)) { New-Item -Path $AmsiPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $AmsiPath -Name "FeatureBits" -Value 2 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-DefenderAmsiSignatureStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-DefenderAmsiSignatureStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-DefenderAmsiSignatureStatus.ps1
$AmsiPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\AMSI"
if (Test-Path $AmsiPath) {
    $AmsiBits = Get-ItemProperty -Path $AmsiPath -Name "FeatureBits" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($AmsiBits -and $AmsiBits.FeatureBits -eq 2) {
        Write-Output "Compliant"
        exit 0
    }
}
Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
exit 1
```

---
